source.label: thm:main
source.quote:
Assume that $
u^\star$ is finitely supported, with expectation $\mu^\star \in (0,1)$ and with support denoted by $\cS^\star$. Let $a \in \cA$ be a suboptimal arm such that $\mu_a > 0$ and $
u_a$ is finitely supported. Then, for all $c_a > 0$ and all $0 < \epsilon < \min\{\Delta_a,  rac{c_a/2}{1+c_a}(1-\mu^\star)\kmin(
u_a,\mu^\star)\}$, the expected number of times the $\kmin$--strategy, run with $f(t)=\log t$, pulls arm $a$ satisfies ...

results.notes: This bounds the expected number of pulls of a single suboptimal arm, not the regret. Kinf_i is taken over finitely supported distributions with mean > mu_star. eps is a free analysis parameter.

conditions: all arm distributions finitely supported on [0,1]

source.quote: As a corollary, we get (by taking some common value for all $c_a$) that for all $c>0$, $\ol{R}_T \leq \sum_{a\in\cA} \Delta_a \frac{(1+c)\log T}{\kmin(\nu_a,\mu^\star)} + h(c)$ ... As a consequence, we recover the asymptotic results ... $\limsup_{T\rightarrow\infty} \frac{\ol{R}_T}{\log T} \leq \sum_{a\in\cA} \frac{\Delta_a}{\kmin(\nu_a,\mu^\star)}$.

results.notes: This is an informal corollary stated in prose. The intermediate finite-time form includes an unspecified constant h(c), so it is not recorded separately. The paper notes that the asymptotic result itself was already known (Burnetas & Katehakis; Honda & Takemura).
